narrative.overview: The site treats "considering Jordy for a role" as a product decision, not a portfolio to browse. It borrows the confident, flat-color, hand-illustrated register of a SaaS landing page (the user's pinned reference, rothfinder.com) and applies it to a person: an off-white paper ground, oversized bold display type, black-outlined cards in saturated flat accent colors, and a stat ledger styled like a scoreboard. The only ornament is a set of thin, single-stroke hand-drawn squiggles that self-draw on load and on scroll — everything else is flat color, hard black-ish outlines, and rounded geometry. The pinned reference used small-caps tracked eyebrow labels throughout; this build ships with none. That is a deliberate, reviewed craft-floor deviation (eyebrows are banned outright), not an oversight — do not reintroduce them to "match the reference" more closely.
keyCharacteristics: Off-white paper ground with near-black ink and a near-black (not pure-black) outline color reused everywhere.
Two shipped accent-card colors (forest, burgundy) out of four defined in tokens; periwinkle and rust exist as unused reserve tokens.
One signature motion device: hand-drawn squiggle doodles that self-draw via stroke-dasharray/stroke-dashoffset.
Scroll-triggered reveal (fade + rise) is scoped to the Hero only — not a generic section-enter treatment.
Bricolage Grotesque for all display/heading/label text, Hanken Grotesk for body — chosen to avoid the Space Grotesk/DM Sans default pairing.

rules.name: The Outline-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every bordered surface (pills, cards, tags, the nav mark) is defined primarily by a ~1.75px near-black outline (--line), not by shadow. Where a shadow is present (--shadow-card), it's a soft ambient lift under the whole card, never the thing that defines the edge.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: No small-caps, letter-spaced-uppercase label sits above a heading anywhere in the build, even though the pinned visual reference uses them. This is a standing prohibition carried from the finish review, not a gap to fill in on the next surface.

rules.name: The One-Shadow Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one ambient card shadow and one CTA-specific glow in the whole system. Don't add new shadow values for new components; reuse --shadow-card or state explicitly why a component needs the CTA glow instead.

dos: Do pair every filled or bordered surface with the same 1.75px near-black outline (--line) — it's the connective tissue between the paper, card, and pill components.
Do keep the Doodle component sparse and low-opacity; it's an accent, not a pattern-fill.
Do use Bricolage Grotesque for anything that functions as a label, stat, or heading, and Hanken Grotesk for anything read as a paragraph.
Do scope the .reveal scroll-fade-and-rise treatment to the Hero's copy and ledger only; it is not a generic section-enter animation to apply everywhere.
donts: Don't add small-caps, tracked-uppercase eyebrow labels above headings anywhere, even though the pinned visual reference (rothfinder.com) uses them — this was banned by the finish review as a craft-floor default, not left out by accident.
Don't introduce hard-offset (non-blurred) drop shadows; the system's only shadow is the soft ambient --shadow-card lift plus the tinted CTA glow.

Don't treat the unused --periwinkle / --rust tokens as a mandate to invent additional project cards just to "use" the palette; add a third/fourth accent card only when a third/fourth real project exists.
Don't reintroduce the brighter, pre-review green (~#3fa92e); #2e7d32 is the canonical primary and exists specifically to clear white-text contrast.
